preview.headline: Rangers Visit Struggling Canucks Seeking Bounce-Back on Coast
preview.summary: The New York Rangers travel to face the Vancouver Canucks on November 14, 2026, looking to capitalize on underlying play that far outpaces their current results. The Canucks enter this matchup mired in a six-game losing streak and searching for answers across nearly every major statistical category.
preview.away_analysis: The Rangers hold a 49.73 Corsi For % and a 52.0 Expected Goals % (12th in the league), showing they routinely control a strong share of play and create quality chances at a robust 2.86 Expected Goals For / 60. However, a major disconnect exists between their process and actual goal production, reflected by a low 40.82 Goals For % and an 8.03% shooting percentage. They feature an elite penalty kill operating at 88.33% (3rd in the league) while taking 3.89 penalties per 60 minutes. Goalie Garand projects to start with a 20th-ranked GSAx over his last 20 games.
preview.home_analysis: The Canucks are fighting through a difficult stretch marked by a six-game losing streak and an extensive four days of rest. Vancouver sits near the bottom of the league in foundational metrics, registering a 44.21 Corsi For % and a 40.37 Expected Goals % (32nd). Their defensive suppression has struggled with 3.06 Expected Goals Against / 60, and their penalty kill sits last in the NHL at 63.08%. Merilainen is projected in goal without a registered GSAx rank in the last 20 games.
matchup_edges: New York holds a massive advantage in expected goals share (52.0% vs. 40.37%) and high-danger chance generation.
The Rangers' elite 3rd-ranked penalty kill (88.33%) matches up favorably against Vancouver's league-worst 32nd-ranked penalty kill (63.08%).
Vancouver enjoys a rest advantage with 4 full calendar days between games compared to New York's 2 days.
preview.x_factor: Canucks discipline and special teams execution. Vancouver's 63.08% penalty kill will be severely tested if they take penalties at their usual rate against a Rangers team looking to unlock suppressed offensive finishing.
preview.key_question: Can the Rangers translate their strong expected goal generation into actual goals against a Canucks team struggling mightily in high-danger suppression?
preview.quick_takeaway: The Rangers hold a distinct advantage in overall possession and high-danger chance control, while the Canucks enter desperately trying to snap a six-game skid despite a substantial rest advantage.

preview.headline: Hot Streaks Collide as Predators Visit Golden Knights
preview.summary: Both the Nashville Predators and Vegas Golden Knights enter this matchup carrying significant momentum, with Nashville riding a six-game winning streak and Vegas winning four straight. The two squads met previously on October 13, 2026, where the Golden Knights secured a 5-2 victory on the road. Both teams feature identical two days of rest heading into the contest.
preview.away_analysis: The Predators bring a red-hot six-game winning streak into Vegas, supported by special teams excellence. Nashville boasts the league's top penalty kill at 89.47% and a strong power play ranking 8th at 26.56%, while taking penalties at a disciplined 3.23 per 60 (ranking 5th). Underlying metrics show a team sitting at a 49.76% Expected Goals % (18th) and a 46.04% Corsi For % (29th), but they generate a healthy 51.56% High Danger Chances % (14th) and convert at a 50.98% Goals For %. Saros anchors the defense with a strong GSAx rank of 4 over his last 20 games.
preview.home_analysis: The Golden Knights are also on a roll with a four-game winning streak and look to repeat their earlier 5-2 head-to-head success against Nashville. Vegas holds a 47.6% Expected Goals % (24th) and a 46.45% Corsi For % (28th), with an expected goals against rate of 2.77 per 60. Their power play operates at an elite 27.87% (ranking 5th), though their penalty kill sits lower at 76.92% (18th). Hill projects in net with a GSAx rank of 18 over his last 20 games.
matchup_edges: Nashville holds a notable advantage on the penalty kill, ranking 1st in the league at 89.47% compared to Vegas at 18th (76.92%).
In net, Nashville's Saros holds a higher recent GSAx ranking (4th) than Vegas's Hill (18th).
Nashville generates a higher share of high-danger chances, ranking 14th in HDCF% (51.56%) compared to Vegas at 21st (49.03%).
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution, particularly how Nashville's top-ranked penalty kill handles Vegas's 5th-ranked power play.
preview.key_question: Can the Predators maintain their high danger chance conversion and special teams dominance to avenge their early-season loss against Vegas?
preview.quick_takeaway: An intriguing clash of surging teams where Nashville brings elite penalty killing and goaltending metrics against a potent Vegas power play, though both sides display remarkably similar overall shot-share numbers.
